title: The Culprit is Genta's Dad
notes: Detective-cast (Conan, Genta, Ayumi, Mitsuhiko, Takagi, Megure, Chiba) omitted by convention -- recurring series regulars, not case-specific to this episode's crime. No `event` node type: actions are direct typed edges. The old lower-fidelity `cases/` file had the culprit right (Gankichi Kojima, s3) but everything else was thin: generic `knows`/`was_at` edges, an `events` array, and a single vague clue ('obscure calligraphy style'). The transcript makes the real mechanism much more specific: Gonsaku secretly ran the whole 'Kojima-san Competition' as a manhunt for the man who beheaded his dog Gonta during a burglary six months earlier (Hyakki Yakou gang) -- push-ups measured shoe size against the burglar's yard footprint, the singing test matched voice against words the gang leader was overheard muttering, and the kanji test's video secretly recorded handedness. All three finalists passed those screens (same distant surname spelling, same shoe size, same left-handedness, similar voice), so Gonsaku set one final trap: a torn washi paper copied from the gang's ransom note, written in a distinctive circular-stroke kanji style. Bunta and Genji both misread it as plain numbers (801 / 108, the latter reported as 'shakuhachi'); only Gankichi read it correctly as kanji ('ippin'), exposing him. The episode's title is itself the misdirection the case is built on: Genta's actual father is Genji (identified only via a Tokyo-dialect hi->shi pronunciation quirk, e.g. 'shakuhachi' for 108 and singing 'Shi no moto' for 'Hi no moto' in Kuroda Bushi), who is innocent -- the real culprit, Gankichi, has no relation to Genta at all. The old file's `has_motive_against` was 'unspecified'; the transcript supplies a clear one (self-preservation/evidence destruction on Gankichi's side, vigilante revenge for the dog on Gonsaku's side). Minor transcript inconsistency: Genji's contestant number is read as 84 in part 1 and 81 in part 2 -- both are given verbatim in the relevant node's attrs. case_type: murder (manslaughter during a struggle, per Gankichi's own confession).
